problem: Embodied Question Answering (EQA) research is fragmented across tasks, datasets and method families, and prior surveys do not systematically relate perception, memory, reasoning and action or audit which datasets actually require exploration or interaction.
motivation: EQA differs from traditional VQA because an agent may have to actively acquire and retain evidence from a 3D environment before answering. A structured view of tasks, methods and capabilities is needed to see which capabilities existing benchmarks really test and where foundation-model approaches fall short.
key_idea: Organize EQA literature with an author-developed PMRA (Perception-Memory-Reasoning-Action) analytical framework and a three-level taxonomy (task formulations, method architectures, capability dimensions), backed by a dataset audit and a semi-systematic review of 72 core papers.
insight: The dataset audit shows that of 20 tabulated datasets only five permit or require active exploration and only one requires physical object interaction, so most benchmarks under-test embodied action. The synthesis identifies explicit memory interfaces and question-conditioned information acquisition as examples of emerging mechanisms, but deliberately does not infer prevalence or trends from publication counts.
method: Corpus selection: semi-systematic review of 72 core papers chosen from 210 candidates, plus a separate qualitative update of 28 additional records through July 2026
PMRA framework: Perception-Memory-Reasoning-Action used as an analytical lens, not a proposed robot-control architecture
Three-level taxonomy: task formulations, method architectures, and capability dimensions
Dataset audit: 20 datasets tabulated with counts recomputed from an extraction sheet (exploration, interaction requirements)
Four architecture-based stages: defined without using publication year as an assignment rule
Outlook: four recurring limitations of foundation-model approaches and nine research directions toward 2030
numbers_note: Survey, abstract only; no experimental results.
results: The survey finds that among 20 audited EQA datasets only five permit or require active exploration and only one requires physical object interaction. It proposes a four-stage architectural categorization and lists four limitations of foundation-model approaches and nine future directions toward 2030.
limitations: Semi-systematic rather than fully systematic selection (72 of 210 candidates); the 28 extra records are only a qualitative update
Does not infer prevalence, temporal growth or relative importance of mechanisms from publication frequencies
PMRA is an author-defined analytical lens, not empirically validated
